item.title: Synthesizing Geographical Semantics and Large Language Model for OD ‐Based Trajectory Captioning
item.description:
Hang Zhou, Shengwen Li, Yaqin Ye, Zhouzheng Xu, Yuxing Wu, Chaofan Fan, Bingyi Li, Hong Yao, et al.
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70425
ABSTRACT Trajectory captioning aims to represent trajectories in natural language texts, providing a human‐friendly approach to understanding and utilizing trajectory data. Previous trajectory captioning methods relied on manually defined rule templates to describe trajectories, failing to accurately and comprehensively capture the trajectory semantics. To address these issues, this paper synthesizes the semantics of the origin and destination (OD) points of trajectories with large language models (LLMs) to improve trajectory captioning. The proposed method first designs a trajectory context augmentation module that enriches the trajectories' context using the spatial information from Point‐of‐Interest (POI) distributions and human travel data from check‐in records. The method develops a geographical semantic‐based reasoning module that constructs a time‐subcategory graph and trains a POI matching module to capture the geographical semantics of the trajectories. Finally, a trajectory decoding module is developed, which leverages LLMs and the Chain‐of‐Thought inspired strategies to generate trajectory captions. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method outperforms baseline methods on both lexical‐overlap and semantic‐alignment metrics. This paper explores a new approach for trajectory semantics representation and provides a methodological reference for the text generation tasks in various geographical applications.

item.title: GIS ‐ MCDA and Uncertainty Analysis for Underground Dam Candidate Zone Prioritization in the Beyşehir and Çumra Subbasins
item.description:
Ahmet Emin Karkınlı, Aslı Bozdağ, Zeynep Ünal, Abdurrahman Lermi
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70424
ABSTRACT Underground dams can support subsurface water storage in water‐scarce basins, but preliminary siting requires the integration of heterogeneous hydrogeological, environmental, and planning factors together with an assessment of spatial decision uncertainty. This study develops a GIS‐based sequential spatial decision‐support framework for prioritizing underground‐dam candidate zones in the Beyşehir and Çumra subbasins of the Konya Closed Basin, Türkiye. Twenty‐one raster factor layers representing hydrological, hydrogeological, geological, topographic, soil, land‐use, climatic, accessibility, and settlement conditions were standardized and integrated using hierarchical AHP weights and weighted linear combination over 2,092,998 valid pixels of an 84.68‐m grid. Criterion redundancy and criterion influence were examined before aggregation: the largest variance inflation factor in the primary criterion set is 4.18, and decomposing the variance of the composite score shows that its spatial pattern is driven mainly by five soil and geology layers, which carry 31.6% of the total weight but produce 77.6% of the spatial variation. The continuous suitability surface was classified using quantile five‐class classification, with observed equal‐interval classification as a control; within‐one‐class agreement between the two classifications was 85.03%, with 45.51% exact agreement. AHP weight uncertainty was examined through 500 Monte Carlo perturbation scenarios, and cells exceeding a fixed reference score in at least 80% of scenarios, covering 254,887.07 ha, were carried forward. After protected land was removed, 1267 contiguous zones were extracted; 156 exceeded a 50 ha minimum‐area threshold and 16 were non‐dominated on suitability, exceedance frequency, and compactness, covering 19,461.56 ha. Groundwater depths at 33 wells showed no significant association with the suitability score and are used as a plausibility check. The framework links criterion redundancy and influence, classification stability, weight uncertainty, spatial contiguity, and planning constraints within a sequential decision‐support workflow.

item.title: Exploring Deep Learning Models for Environmental Optimization in Morel Mushroom Cultivation
item.description:
Chunji Zhang, Dan Liu
Transactions in GIS, vol. 30, issue 7
DOI: 10.1111/tgis.70359
ABSTRACT Morchella mushrooms ( Morchella spp.) are highly valued edible fungi due to their distinctive flavor and medicinal benefits. However, their artificial cultivation remains challenging because growth is extremely sensitive to environmental fluctuations and complex interactions among soil, moisture, and temperature. Conventional control approaches are largely manual, inefficient, and unable to respond dynamically to microclimatic variations, resulting in unstable yields. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Hybrid Deep Environmental Optimization Framework (HyDEOF) that integrates Deep Belief Networks (DBN) with an Adaptive Neuro‐Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) for intelligent environmental regulation during Morel cultivation. DBN models nonlinear patterns from sensor data, while ANFIS enables real‐time adaptive control of humidity, CO 2 concentration, and soil temperature. Experimental results from controlled cultivation chambers demonstrate that HyDEOF improves yield consistency by 21%, reduces energy consumption by 19%, and enhances substrate moisture retention by 17% compared with conventional systems, highlighting its potential for sustainable and efficient Morel production. Key stressors influencing Morel cultivation include humidity fluctuation, CO 2 imbalance, and soil temperature variability, critically affecting fruiting stability. The methodology utilizes sensor‐based environmental data collection using DBN‐based feature extraction and ANFIS‐based adaptive control within a closed loop system. This approach is tested using experimental studies that evaluate environmental stability, productivity, and energy consumption.
